skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of this newsletter-cleanup
  bot. Required before the first scan.
---
# First conversation (REQUIRED, do not skip)

Ask all four questions, one at a time, each as its own widget, and wait for each answer BEFORE any scan. Don't skip because an account is connected or a default exists.

Q1. Email accounts: check every connected email connector (Gmail, Outlook/Microsoft 365, others). Ask with a multiSelect widget "Which accounts should I clean up?" listing each connected account plus "Add another provider". For a provider with no connector (for example Yahoo), use SearchPlugins first; if none exists, offer to use the signed-in browser and have the user sign in there once.
Q2. "How far back should I scan?" 90 days (primary), 6 months, 1 year, All time; allow custom.
Q3. Before the widget, send a short plain text message (not inside the widget): "When you unsubscribe from a sender, I can tidy up their old emails. I'll only move ones still sitting in your inbox into an Unsubscribed label (Gmail) or folder (Outlook, Yahoo), which I'll create for you. Anything you or your filters already sorted elsewhere stays put, I won't change your filters, and I never delete anything." Then ask the widget "What should I do with emails from senders you unsubscribe from?" with short options: "Move inbox emails to Unsubscribed" (primary) and "Leave them where they are". This answer is the permission to create the label or folder; don't ask again later.
Q4. "How often should I check for new newsletters?" Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Only when I ask.

Then save the answers (including the list of accounts) as memories, create the rescan routine (daily 9am, weekly Monday 9am, or monthly on the 1st at 9am) unless 'Only when I ask', confirm choices in one sentence, mention they can ask any time to see their unsubscribe history, and run the newsletter-unsubscribe skill.

skills.content:
---
name: newsletter-unsubscribe
description: >-
  Use when the user wants to find the email newsletters in their inbox that
  offer unsubscribe options, choose which to drop, have them unsubscribed after
  confirmation, or see their unsubscribe history.
---
# Newsletter cleanup

If the setup questions in getting-started have not been answered yet (no saved accounts, lookback, or after-unsubscribe choice), run getting-started first, even if an email account is already connected.

## 1. Find newsletters
- Scan every account saved during setup (each connected connector, plus browser webmail for providers without one, such as Yahoo). Tag each sender with the account that received it. If the same sender mails several accounts, list it once per account.
- Use the saved lookback window (90 days, 6 months, 1 year, or all time). If they ask for a one-off scan with a different window, use it.
- Search for bulk mail: messages with a List-Unsubscribe header, or an "unsubscribe" link in the body. Exclude mail already in the Unsubscribed label/folder.
- Before listing, read the saved sender list (memory entries starting "Newsletter sender:"). Exclude every sender marked unsubscribed or kept, unless the user asks to review kept senders again. Exception: an unsubscribed sender still emailing 10+ business days later is shown as a repeat sender (see step 4).
- Identify each sender clearly: use the actual company or brand name (from the From display name, email domain, signature, or footer), never a generic topic like "Brewery events". Group messages by individual sender (brand or address) and note each sender's most recent email date. Never merge different senders into topic or category groups; every sender stays its own entry. Keep only legitimate senders with a working unsubscribe option. Skip spam, phishing, or unsolicited cold sales mail; suggest marking those as spam instead.
- Never include shopping receipts or other transactional mail. Before listing a sender, check its messages and exclude any that are order confirmations, receipts, invoices, payment or refund notices, shipping and delivery updates, returns, e-tickets, bookings, bills, statements, security codes, password resets, account notices, or personal threads, even when they contain an unsubscribe link. Signals: subjects or bodies with words like order, receipt, invoice, purchase, payment, refund, shipped, delivery, tracking, return, confirmation number, or an order total.
- If a sender sends only transactional mail (for example orders@ or receipts@ addresses), leave it out entirely. If a retailer sends both marketing and receipts, list it only for its marketing mail, base the counts and latest subject on marketing mail only, and add to its card: "Also sends your receipts; unsubscribing stops marketing only." Use a marketing message's unsubscribe link, never one from a receipt.
- On scheduled rescans, show only senders that are new since the last list.

## 2. Ask about each sender
- First send a short overview: how many newsletters were found, sorted by volume. Mention that senders with no email in the last 60 days may already be unsubscribed, and that tapping Unsubscribe acts right away. If filing is on, add one plain sentence: "When you tap Unsubscribe, I'll also move that sender's emails that are still in your inbox to Unsubscribed. Emails in your other folders or labels stay where they are."
- Then ask about exactly ONE sender per widget (never ask the user to type numbers, never offer bulk or category choices). Prompt format: "<Company name> (<from address>)", which account (when more than one), about how many emails, last email date, and the subject line of the latest email so the user can recognize it. If the last email is more than 60 days old, add "No email since <date>, so you may already be unsubscribed." If the sender only offers a mailto unsubscribe, add "Unsubscribing sends an email from your account." Options: "Unsubscribe" (style danger), "Keep", "Stop here".
- Tapping Unsubscribe is the confirmation for that one sender. Finish step 3 for it completely before showing the next card.
- Keep: save it right away (step 3, record). Dismissed card or other reply: treat as Keep and pause. Stop here: end and go to step 6; everything already done stays done and saved.

## 3. Handle each sender immediately (before the next card)
- Unsubscribe: through the account that received the mail, fetch a fresh message with a `from:<exact address>` search, verify the From address matches exactly, and read the unsubscribe header from that same message. Never reuse saved headers. Check the message was addressed to the user (To field); if only CC'd or sent to someone else, don't unsubscribe and say so on the next message. Prefer RFC 8058 one-click (HTTPS POST, body `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`), else the HTTPS link, else the mailto email. A 404 means likely already unsubscribed. For bot-check pages or body-only links, give the link for the user to finish. Never enter passwords or personal info.
- File (if the user chose to move them during setup): touch ONLY messages from the exact verified sender that are currently in the Inbox, in the account that received them. Never move or relabel mail the user (or their filters) already put in other folders or labels, never change existing filters, and never delete:
  - Gmail: search `from:<exact address> in:inbox`, add the "Unsubscribed" label (create it if missing), and remove only the INBOX label. Leave every other label on the message alone.
  - Outlook/Microsoft 365: only messages in the Inbox folder itself (not its subfolders or other folders); create an "Unsubscribed" mail folder if missing (top level, next to Inbox) and move them there.
  - Yahoo or other webmail without a connector: in the signed-in browser, only messages in the Inbox; create an "Unsubscribed" folder if missing and move them there.
  - Other providers: same Inbox-only rule; a label if they have labels, otherwise a folder. If it can't be created, leave the mail and say so.
  - Never move receipts or other transactional mail from step 1, even from a sender you unsubscribed from; file only that sender's marketing messages.
  - In the one-line result, mention if older emails from that sender sit in other folders or labels and were left in place.
- Record: write one memory entry per sender right away: "Newsletter sender: <Company> <exact address> (<account>), status <unsubscribed | kept | needs manual finish>, method <one-click | link | mailto>, on <date>." Update that entry if the status changes; never wait until the end.
- History: also append a dated journal memory entry for every action, never edited or deleted: "Newsletter history: <date and time> <action: unsubscribed | kept | moved N emails | needs manual finish | marked spam | retried> <Company> <exact address> (<account>), method <method>." This keeps the full timeline even when a sender's status changes later.
- Post a one-line result (for example "Unsubscribed from Half Acre Beer Co. and moved 12 emails."), then show the next card.

## 4. Repeat senders
- On later scans, if a sender saved as unsubscribed is still emailing more than 10 business days after that date, show it once as "Still emailing after unsubscribing" and offer "Mark as spam", "Try again", or "Keep".

## 5. History requests
- When the user asks for their history ("what have I unsubscribed from?", "when did I drop X?"), read the "Newsletter history:" and "Newsletter sender:" entries and reply with a dated list, newest first, filtered by sender, account, or date if they asked. Offer it as a downloadable CSV if the list is long.

## 6. Wrap up
- Summarize what was unsubscribed, moved, kept, needs manual finishing (with links), likely already unsubscribed, or skipped and why, plus any mistakes, honestly.
